subject: general
question: Two trains start at the same time from A and B and move towards each other at the rates of 10 km/h and 27 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 340 km more than the other. The distance between A and B is _______.
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of first train = 10 km/h

Speed of second train = 27 km/h

The difference in distances covered = 340 km

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time.

**Concept used**:

When two trains are moving towards each other, the relative speed is the sum of their speeds. &
